To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
moderately doped junctionless MOSFETS perform significantly better than highly doped devices.

the use of a moderate channel doping concentration of ~1018 cm− 3 in ultra low power junctionless double gate MOSFETS results in better performance than the use of higher doping concentration of ~ 1019 cm− 3.
the channel doping concentration of the junctionless (J-L) MOSFETs should be reduced to 1x1018 cm-3 to achieve better low power performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and optimization of junctionless MOSFETS (JL-MOSFETs) for ultra low power applications.
the study of low power junctionless (J-L) double gate MOS transistors for subthreshold circuit design.
the design of a low power junctionless (JLT) MOSFET.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
moderately doped junctionless transistors are more suitable for low power applications than heavily doped devices.
moderate doping (1018 cm3) in JL transistors is a more suitable design for subthreshold ULP applications.
moderately doped JL transistors are the best suited for ULP sub-threshold logic applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
moderate channel doping and gate workfunction engineering are key design parameters for realizing improved ULP performance for junctionless devices.
moderate doping (1018 cm–3), gate workfunction of ~ 4.8eV, and source/drain extension implantation away from gate edge would be ideal for low power JL MOSFET design.
the requirement of high channel doping is not a necessity for low power applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the channel doping concentration in JL devices can be lowered to 1018 cm-3 for ULP applications without compromising device performance.
the requirement of high channel doping for JL MOSFET design can be relaxed for subthreshold logic applications without compromising device performance.
a moderate channel doping concentration (≤1018 cm− 3) can lead to improved ULP performance metrics for JL MOSFET design.
